body:
In article <36FB707A.178E@mail.saber.net>,
  scorey@saber.net wrote:
> minga4@my-dejanews.com included:
>
> >
> > Both perpetrators are intent on "proving" to the reader that they are who
> > they say they are...  A mathemetician is intent on "proving" his theories.
> > Classic for Dr. Kaczynski...  Additionally,(and just another 'small' snippet
> > of similarity) you might note in the style of writing, that both Kaczynski
> > and Zodiac phrase their use of "...I & the police..."  and  "...us and the
> > FBI..." instead of saying correctly, "...the police & I..."  or  "...the FBI
> > and us(we)..."
>
> 	This particular aspect of grammar has always confused me.  My best
> recollection is that "I" must come after the other noun (in this case,
> "the police") only if it is the subject of the sentence.  Otherwise, the
> order is indifferent.  If that is so, what FC and Z have in common is a
> remembrance of junior high grammar that common use ignores, and even
> well educated people tend to forget.  If that is not so, I am just
> wrong, which would not surprise me a bit.
>
>
> Scott


Scott:

I agree with you that the transposition as described is a common one and a
mistake that many people make; however, in adding this to the other stylistic
comparisons of writings between Unabomber and Zodiac, you might conclude that
their writings are indeed strikingly similar...  (Check these out - from
http://members.bellatlantic.net/~mignarda)


No. 1:  (Use of "...On top of...")
Z:   I shall (on top of every thing else) torture all 13 of my slaves
      that I have wateing for me in Paradice. Mikado Letter,
      1970.
                    K:   On top of these, I attached on the side of the pipe
                         with strapping tape a layer of small nails. On top of
                         everything I wrapped the pipe with friction tape ....
                         GX18-2033, pp.236-241.

No. 2    (Use of '...this:...')
Z:   The reason that Im writing to the Times is this, They dont bury me on the
     back pages like some of the others. L.A. Times Letter, 1971.

  K:  London's idea is, briefly, this: Let us not attempt to  interfere  with
the development of behavioral technology  .... 1971Essay  K:  The other, and
the one that I advocate, is this: In  simple terms, stop scientific progress
by withdrawing	all major sources of research funds. 1971 Essay.  K:  But the
point is this: If there is such a solution, no	one at present seems to know
just what it is. 1971 Essay.

No. 3  (Use of '...blast...'
Z:   I hope you enjoy your selves when I have my Blast. Jolly
      Roger Card.
                   K:  For these reasons, I want to get my revenge in one big
                     blast. GX18-2003F, p. 11.

No. 4  (Use of '...trigger mech...' Z:	At the moment the children are safe
from the bomb because  it is so massive to dig in & the triger mech requires
much  work to get it adjusted just right. Belli Letter, 1969.  K:  Its no fun
having to spend all your evenings and weekends	preparing dangerous mixtures,
filing trigger mechanisms  out of scraps of metal .... New York Times Letter,
1995.

No. 5  (Use of '...busy work...') Z:  I gave the cops som bussy work to do to
keep them happy.  Seven-Page Letter, 1969.  K:	This seems to us a thoroughly
contemptible way for the  human race to end up, and we doubt that many people
 would find fulfilling lives in such pointless busy-work.  Unabomber
Manifesto, 1995.

No.6  (Use of  '...dangerous animal..." - hunting is 'very exciting -
thrilling) Z:  It is more fun than killing wild game in the forrest because 
man is the most dangerou[s] anamal of all. To kill something  gives me the
most thrilling exper[i]ence. Three-Part Cipher,  1969.	K:  I drove up to
Humboldt county for deer hunting.... deer  hunting is very exciting. Turchie
Affidavit, Addendum,  1996.  K:  He knew how to protect himself from heat,
cold, rain,  dangerous animals, etc. Unabomber, Manifesto, 1995.


No. 7  (Need to "...prove...")
Z:    This is the murderer of the 2 teenagers last Christmass at
       Lake Herman & the girl on the 4th of July near the golf
       course in Vallejo. To prove I killed them I shall state some
       facts which only I & the police know. Three-Part Cipher,
       1969.
Z:    I am the murderer of the taxi driver over by Washington St.
       & Maple St. last night, to prove this here is a blood stained
       piece of his shirt. Stine Letter, 1969.
Z:   To prove that I am the Zodiac, Ask the Vallejo cop about
       my electric gun sight .... Seven-Page Letter, 1969.

  K:  To prove that we are the ones who planted the bomb at U.	Of Cal. last
May we will mention a few details that could  be known only to us and the FBI
who investigated the  incident.  S.F. Examiner Letter, 1985.  K:  This is a
message from the terrorist group FC. To prove  its authenticity we give our
identifying number .... New  York Times Letter, 1995.  K:  To prove that the
writer of this letter knows something  about FC, the first two digits of
their identifying  number are 55.  S.F. Chronicle Threat Letter, 1995.

No. 8 (Request or demand for publication)
Z:  This letter should be published for all to read it. Typewritten
    Letter, 1966.
                   K:  We encourage you to print this letter. New York Times
                       Letter, 1995.

No. 9  (association of motorycycles/noise-makers)
  Z:  The S.F. Police could have caught me last night if they had
       searched the park properly instead of holding road races
       with their motor cicles seeing who could make the most
       noise. The car drivers should have just parked their cars &
       sat there quietly waiting for me to come out of cover. Stine
       Letter, 1969.
                   K: For example, a variety of noise-making devices: power
                      mowers, radios, motorcycles, etc. If the use of these
                      devices is unrestricted, people who want peace and quiet
                      are frustrated by the noise. Manifesto, 1995.
                   K: When I see a motorcyclist tearing up the mountain
                      meadows... I want to kick him in the face while he is
                      dying. GX-2003F, p. 11.

No. 10  (Use of the word '...fun...')
Z:   I like killing people because it is so much fun. Three-Part
     Cipher, 1969.
Z:   I was in this phone booth haveing some fun with the Vallejo
     cop when he was walking by. August, 1969 Letter.
Z:   Have fun!! By the way it could be rather messy if you try to
     bluff me. Seven-Page Letter, 1969.
Z:   PS I hope you have fun trying to figure out who I killed[.]
     Thirteen-Symbol Cipher, 1970.
Z:   Yes I shall have great fun inflicting the most delicious of pain
     to my Slaves. Mikado Letter, 1970.

  K:  At first he will have a lot of fun, but by and by he will  become
acutely bored and demoralized. Manifesto, 1995.  K:  [I]t's more fun to watch
the entertainment put out by the  media than to read a sober essay.
Manifesto, 1995.  K:  Its no fun having to spend all your evenings and
weekends  preparing dangerous mixtures .... New York Times Letter,  1995.

No.11  (Use of word 'So' to begin sentences) Z:  So don't make it to easy for
me. Typewritten Letter, 1966. Z:  So I shall change the way the collecting of
slaves.Seven-Page Letter, 1969. Z:  So as you can see the police don't have
much to work on.  Seven-Page Letter, 1969. Z:  So now I have a little list
... Little List Letter, 1970.

  K:  So we expect to be able to pack deadly bombs into ... more  harmless
looking packages. New York Times Letter, 1995.	K:  So we offer a bargain.
New York Times Letter, 1995.  K:  So if you take the trouble to read our
manuscript ... Tom  Tyler Letter, 1995.  K:  So we are left with the
question: What kind of legislative  program would have a chance of saving
freedom? 1971  Essay.  K:  So certain artificial needs have been created ... 
Manifesto, 1995.  K:  So modern man's drive for security tends ... Manifesto,
 1995.	K:  So they always feel hard-pressed financially ...  Manifesto,
1995.  K:  So we present these principles ... Manifesto, 1995.	K:  So they
send him to Sylvan. Manifesto, 1995.

No. 12 (mention of gun-control & ban on guns)  Another interesting fact in
this  similarity is that these two correspondences were written within approx
 one month of each other. Z:  [M]y killing tools have been boughten through
the mail order	outfits before the ban went into efect. [E]xcept one & it was
 bought out of the state. Seven-Page Letter, November 9, 1969.	K:  The
stricter gun control laws recommended by the U.S.  Commission on Violence are
a case in point. Letter to  Chicago Daily News, December 14, 1969.

No. 13 (discussion of torture (Z) ; torture in most fiendish of manner(K)) Z:
 I shall (on top of every thing else) torture all 13 of my slaves  that I
have wateing for me in Paradice. Some I shall tie over	ant hills and watch
them scream & twich and squirm. Others	shall have pine splinters driven
under their nails & then  burned. Others shall be placed in cages & fed salt
beef untill  they are gorged then I shall listen to their pleass for water
and  I shall laugh at them. Others will hang by their thumbs & burn  in the
sun then I will rub them down deep heat to warm them  up. Others I shall skin
them alive & let them run around  screaming. The Mikado Letter, 1970.  K:  I
hadn't previously been troubled by rats around here, but  I just discovered
that my pack has been chewed up so badly  that it is nearly ruined ... This
means some deadfalls are  going to be set. I hope I catch one of those
[expletive]  alive--I will torture it to death in the most fiendish  manner I

>The above-style comparison is very similar to the one done by the FBI in

comparing known Kaczynski writings to the Unabomber's Manifesto & other
letters written to the press and/or victims.  This, combined with other
similarities/connections, helped to identify the Unabomber as Ted Kaczynski
and lead to his arrest.

Now, by adding these similarities in writing style to the multiplying list of
other connections (see below to name a few from Dr. Zodiac CD by Oswell &
Rusconi), these similarities in writing style of both the Zodiac and
Unabomber appear to me to be quite extraordinary:

Now it's me that's rambling...     Minga!
